main_evidence: Independent Mann-Kendall, Sen slope and BH-FDR recomputation
Remove each year from 2015-2025 and recompute trends
result: Mean Sen-slope Spearman=0.903; mean direction agreement=92.98%
interpretation: Absolute historical trend ordering is generally stable, with sensitivity to endpoint years.

main_evidence: Independent reproduction, leave-one-year-out and threshold sensitivity
result: Independent reproduction=100%; mean LOO class agreement=82.67%; mean threshold agreement=92.61%
interpretation: Trajectory classification is reproducible and reasonably robust, but temporally sensitive when endpoint years are removed.

main_evidence: History-only Sen slope compared with subsequent 3-year change
interpretation: Historical slope direction should NOT be used as a forecast of subsequent warming or cooling direction.

main_evidence: History-only trajectory classes evaluated against next-year actual heat
result: Hot-side grids were on average 1.845 C hotter; Top-25% heat risk ratio=3.44x
interpretation: Trajectory classes provide meaningful evidence of subsequent relative heat burden.
